newsitem.title: USA: S. Africa's Manuel endorses May 7 CME rand launch.
newsitem.headline: S. Africa's Manuel endorses May 7 CME rand launch.

text.p: South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel on Thursday endorsed next week's launch of rand futures and options on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, saying the products were a sign of South Africa's integration into the world economy.
"The preparations for the launch of rand futures contracts on the Merc are a very, very exciting part of this globalization," Manuel told a news conference.

The CME on May 7 will launch rand futures and options on the CME's Growth and Emerging Markets division, and the South Africa Futures Exchange (SAFEX) will launch an inverse product the same day. A dollar/rand futures product was listed recently on FINEX, the financial products division of the New York Cotton Exchange, and trades in New York and Dublin.

"The key questions for us (are) about the integration of the South African economy into the global economy," said Manuel. "It's a path we've pursued quite vigorously from the time of the elections of 1994."
After growth of around three percent a year in 1994 through 1996, Trevor forecast South Africa's economy would grow by six percent a year beginning in 2000.
This outlook, after South Africa's recent relaxation of foreign exchange controls, makes the rand a viable product for the CME, exchange officials said.
"We see South Africa as being a part of the tapestry of the world economy," CME chairman Jack Sandner said.
Rick Kilcollin, CME president, said the rand contract was a risk management tool for the growing South African markets.
"Johannesburg is the 16th largest stock exchange in the world...and real interest rates are very attractive in South Africa, and that's generating a lot of interest to investors," Kilcollin said.
Rand futures and options will be "very beneficial to all the participants in the market as a way of managing currency exposure associated with investment in South Africa," Kilcollin said.
The CME rand contracts will be sized at 500,000 rand -- about $112,000 at current levels -- and will be quoted in dollars per rand. The minimum price increment of $0.000025 equals $12.50.
Sandner said he hoped arbitrage would develop between the SAFEX and CME rand products.
New Zealand dollar futures and options will also begin trading at the CME on May 7.
